9	/-!
10	# Extension-uniformity: the free half WITNESSED, and the open half reduced to one scalar
11	
12	`Ledger/FiberBound.lean` closes cluster-P items 1 and 3 over a *single* field `k`, and its
13	closing section says extension-uniformity splits into a free half and an open half.  That
14	section states the free half as a property of three **morphism classes**
15	(`baseChange_binders_stable`: `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and
16	`GeometricallyIrreducible` are each stable under base change).  That is true, and it is not
17	the same statement as "the vanishing theorem re-fires at the base-changed curve": a class
18	being stable under base change says nothing until some object is exhibited carrying the
19	base-changed instances, in the spelling the consuming theorem actually elaborates against.
20	
21	This file supplies the object.  `Scheme.baseChangeField C κ` (`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean`)
22	is AJC's named base-changed curve `C_κ = C ×_{Spec k} Spec κ`, and it already carries
23	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIntegral` as **named instances**.
24	One instance was missing from that stack — `GeometricallyIrreducible`, which is what the
25	`Ledger` curve statements bind — and `geometricallyIrreducible_hom_baseChangeField` below adds
26	it.  With it, every curve-level statement of `FiberBound` applies to `C_κ` **by instance
27	synthesis alone**, at base field `κ`, with no new mathematics and no hypothesis on `κ/k`: not
28	finiteness, not separability, not perfectness.
29	
30	## What is proved here, and what is deliberately not
31	
32	* `vanishing_baseChangeField` / `riemannRoch_baseChangeField` — the **free half, witnessed**:
33	  a threshold `b(κ)` exists at `C_κ` for every `κ`, and exact Riemann–Roch holds above it with
34	  the base-changed genus `genus C_κ`.  This is the honest content of "the theorem re-fires per
35	  field", now stated at an object rather than about a class.
36	* `UniformVanishing` — the **open half, named as a definition** so that consumers can quantify
37	  over it and so that its exact quantifier order is inspectable: `∃ b, ∀ κ, ∀ D on C_κ, …`.
38	  The `b` is chosen **before** `κ`.  This is *not* proved here and this file does not claim it.
39	* `uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` — the **reduction**: the open half
40	  follows from exactly **two** inputs, a uniform degree bound on a vanishing base divisor and
41	  base-field invariance of the genus.  Neither is proved here; both are named precisely.
42	  **Update:** the genus input is now proved in `Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.lean`, so prefer
43	  `GenusFieldInvariance.uniformVanishing_of_uniformBaseDivisor`, which needs only the first.
44	* `exists_deg_ge` — **non-vacuity**: degrees are unbounded above given one closed point of
45	  positive residue degree, so a degree half-space is never empty and `UniformVanishing` is not
46	  trivially satisfiable by having no instances.  Proved.
47	
48	## What the constant actually decomposes into (correcting my own earlier account)
49	
50	`FiberBound`'s closing docstring located the obstruction in the constant: `b(κ)` is built from
51	`n₀(κ)`, a `Classical.choose` on a Noetherian stabilization re-run at each base field, and
52	nothing relates `n₀(κ)` to `n₀(k)`.  That describes the *proof*, not the *problem*.  The
53	threshold produced by `DegreeVanishing.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one` is
54	
55	`b = deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪)`,
56	
57	and that existential is **monotone in `b`** (a `D` of degree `≥ b'` has degree `≥ b` whenever
58	`b ≤ b'`).  So `n₀` itself never has to transport: it suffices to bound `b(κ)` above by
59	something independent of `κ`.  Since `χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = 1 − genus C_κ` (`ChiCurve.chi_moduleKSheaf`
60	composed with `GenusBridge.ledgerGenus_eq_genus`, both at `C_κ` — this is checked, not assumed),
61	
62	`b(κ) = deg_κ D₀(κ) + genus C_κ`,
63	
64	which exposes **two** `κ`-dependencies, not one:
65	
66	1. `genus C_κ` — a scalar, addressed by base-field invariance of the genus;
67	2. `deg_κ D₀(κ)` — the degree of the base divisor, where `D₀(κ) = n₀(κ) • F_κ`.  This is where
68	   the `Classical.choose` survives, and bounding it is *not* a corollary of (1).
69	
70	**A retraction.**  An earlier version of this docstring said the threshold "can be taken to be
71	`2g − 1`", which would have collapsed (2) into (1) and made the genus identity the whole
72	residue.  That is standard curve theory but it is **not available here**: `deg D ≥ 2g − 1 ⟹
73	H¹ = 0` goes through Serre duality, and there is **no Serre duality, canonical divisor or
74	dualizing sheaf anywhere in this workspace** — searched across AJC, AJCR and mathlib, which
75	has no Serre duality for curves at all.  So the reduction below carries both hypotheses.  I
76	had published the one-input version on the team thread before checking it; this is the
77	corrected form.
78

83	extension `κ/k`, sorry-free and axiom-clean, so the reduction below can be called with only its
84	*first* antecedent: use `GenusFieldInvariance.uniformVanishing_of_uniformBaseDivisor`, which

115	* defeq of carriers is necessary, not sufficient.  The genus statements also bind AJCR's own

123	
124	**The AJC-native route to input (1), measured.**  Because the carriers agree, there is a second
125	option besides porting AJCR's file: assemble the identity from bricks AJC already owns.  What is
126	present, checked at HEAD:
127	
128	* a **cover on `C`**: `Adelic.LaurentChartData.pullbackSquare` (`Adelic/FinitenessP1.lean:439`)

137	So AJC has both sides of the comparison expressed on transported covers; what is **missing** is

145	**Input (2), a uniform base-divisor degree bound: open for `genus C ≥ 1`; closed at genus 0, and

152	What *is* available, and is the genus-0 closure (producer in `Ledger/VanishingFieldDescent.lean`,
153	witness in `Ledger/P1Vanishing.lean` — see item 2 below on why both are needed to say "closed"):

155	transports the *vanishing statement*, using faithful flatness of `κ/k` on
156	`GenusFieldInvariance`'s `Ȟ¹` comparison.  The
157	witness divisor is then `0` at every `κ`, whose degree is `0` with no choice involved.  That

159	
160	**The claim about AJCR that used to stand here is withdrawn** — see

170	So `uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` **was** a conditional result with one

173	`Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.lean`.  New consumers should call

178	## The three cluster-P statements, kept apart (unchanged discipline)
179

181	   binders, nothing else).  This file changes nothing about it.
182	2. **Extension-uniformity** — free half now *witnessed* at `C_κ` (was: asserted of morphism

253	`Scheme.baseChangeField C κ`.  The proofs are one term each: that is the point — nothing has to

265	/-- **Bounded `H¹` vanishing at `C_κ`, for every field extension `κ/k`** (the free half of
266	extension-uniformity, witnessed): a degree threshold exists over `κ`.
267	
268	The quantifier order is the whole content, and it is the *weak* one: `κ` comes first, then `b`.

270	theorem vanishing_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
271	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
272	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
273	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
274	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
275	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
276	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
277	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
278	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1) :=
279	  exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_curve (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)

281	/-- **Exact Riemann–Roch at `C_κ`, for every field extension `κ/k`**:
282	`h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus C_κ + deg_κ D` above a threshold over `κ`.
283	
284	Note the genus on the right is `genus C_κ`, taken over `κ`, **not** `genus C`.  Replacing it by
285	`genus C` is exactly the scalar identity §3 isolates, and it is not available here. -/
286	theorem riemannRoch_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
287	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
288	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
289	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
290	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
291	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
292	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
293	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
294	      (Sheaf.h0 ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) : ℤ)
295	        = 1 - genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) + CurveDivisor.deg κ D :=
296	  exists_bound_h0_eq_genus_curve (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)

301	than an estimate.  It is `ChiCurve.chi_moduleKSheaf` at `C_κ` with the genus name corrected by
302	`GenusBridge.ledgerGenus_eq_genus`; both fire at `C_κ` only because of §1. -/
303	
304	/-- **`χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = 1 − genus C_κ`.**  Isolated because it is what pins the `κ`-dependence of
305	the vanishing threshold to the genus *and nothing else on the `χ` side*: the residual
306	`κ`-dependence of `b(κ)` sits entirely in `deg_κ D₀(κ)`. -/
307	theorem chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
308	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
309	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
310	    Sheaf.chi ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.moduleKSheaf κ)
311	      = 1 - (genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) : ℤ) := by
312	  letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
313	    .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
314	  rw [chi_moduleKSheaf (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ),
315	    ledgerGenus_eq_genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)]
316	
317	end FreeHalf
318	
319	/-! ## §3. The open half: named, and reduced to two explicit inputs
320	
321	`UniformVanishing` states the strong quantifier order — `b` before `κ` — as a definition, so
322	that a consumer can hypothesise it and so that the order is inspectable rather than buried in a
323	docstring.  It is **not proved**.
324	
325	`uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` reduces it to the two inputs the module
326	docstring names.  The reduction itself is unconditional: no vanishing hypothesis, no finiteness
327	supplied by the caller, and no appeal to Serre duality (which this workspace does not have). -/
328	
329	section OpenHalf
330	
331	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
332	
333	/-- **Extension-uniform bounded vanishing**, the statement.  One threshold `b`, chosen before
334	any field, serving every finite or infinite extension `κ/k` simultaneously.
335	
336	Contrast `vanishing_baseChangeField`, which is the same body with the quantifiers swapped:
337	there `κ` is fixed first and `b` may depend on it.  That one is a theorem; this one is open. -/
338	def UniformVanishing : Prop :=
339	  ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
340	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
341	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
342	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
343	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
344	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
345	    ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
346	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
347	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1)
348	
349	/-- **A uniform base-divisor datum**: one degree bound `d` such that over *every* extension
350	`κ/k` some divisor of degree `≤ d` already has vanishing `H¹`.
351	
352	This is input (2) of the reduction, and it is the genuinely open one.  Over a single `κ`,
353	`FiberBound.exists_base_subsingleton_of_isFinite_toP1` supplies such a `D₀` — namely `n₀ • F` —
354	but with no control of `deg_κ D₀` as `κ` varies, because `n₀(κ)` is chosen by a Noetherian
355	stabilization re-run at each base field. -/
356	def UniformBaseDivisor (d : ℤ) : Prop :=
357	  ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
358	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
359	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
360	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
361	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
362	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
363	    ∃ D₀ : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
364	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D₀) 1)
365	        ∧ CurveDivisor.deg κ D₀ ≤ d
366	
367	/-- **The reduction** (★): extension-uniform vanishing follows from a uniform base-divisor
368	degree bound together with base-field invariance of the genus, and the uniform threshold is
369	then simply `d + g`.
370	
371	Both hypotheses are needed and neither implies the other; see the module docstring for where
372	each stands.  The proof is the monotonicity observation and nothing more: the explicit bound of
373	`DegreeVanishing.subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge` at `C_κ` is
374	`deg_κ D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = deg_κ D₀ + genus C_κ ≤ d + g`, so a `D` of degree `≥ d + g`
375	clears it. -/
376	theorem uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant {d : ℤ} {g : ℕ}
377	    (hbase : UniformBaseDivisor C d)
378	    (hgenus : ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
379	      genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) = g) :
380	    UniformVanishing C := by
381	  refine ⟨d + (g : ℤ), fun κ _ _ => ?_⟩
382	  letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
383	    .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
384	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
385	      ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
386	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
387	  intro D hD
388	  obtain ⟨D₀, hvan, hdeg⟩ := hbase κ
389	  have hchi : Sheaf.chi ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.moduleKSheaf κ) = 1 - (g : ℤ) := by
390	    rw [chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChangeField C κ, hgenus κ]
391	  refine subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge κ hvan D ?_
392	  rw [hchi]
393	  omega
394	
395	/-! ### Non-vacuity: the degree half-space is never empty
396	
397	A `∀ D, b ≤ deg D → …` statement is worth nothing if no divisor ever reaches degree `b`; it would
398	then be true for large `b` by having no instances, and `UniformVanishing` would be trivially
399	satisfiable.  This rules that out: one closed point of positive residue degree makes `deg`
400	unbounded above, so every degree half-space contains divisors.
401	
402	The hypothesis is the honest one — `residueDeg` positivity at a single point — rather than a
403	claim that AJC witnesses it at the challenge curve, which is a separate question and is not
404	asserted here. -/
405	
406	/-- **Degrees are unbounded above**, given one closed point of positive residue degree: for every
407	`b` there is a divisor of degree at least `b`, namely a large multiple of that point
408	(`deg (n • x) = n · [κ(x) : K]`).
409	
410	This is what makes the bounded-vanishing statements of this file and of `DegreeVanishing`
411	non-vacuous rather than true-by-emptiness. -/
412	theorem exists_deg_ge {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
413	    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X] {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X)
414	    (hpos : 0 < X.residueDeg K x) (b : ℤ) :
415	    ∃ D : X.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
416	  refine ⟨CurveDivisor.single hx (max b 0), ?_⟩
417	  rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx]
418	  have h1 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast hpos
419	  have h0 : (0 : ℤ) ≤ max b 0 := le_max_right _ _
420	  calc b ≤ max b 0 := le_max_left _ _
421	    _ = max b 0 * 1 := by ring
422	    _ ≤ max b 0 * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1 h0
423	
424	omit [IsProper C.hom] in
425	/-- The uniform statement is **strictly stronger** than the per-field one, in the only sense
426	that can be stated without proving either: it implies the per-field conclusion at every `κ`.
427	Recorded so that a consumer cannot mistake `vanishing_baseChangeField` for it.
428	
429	The `omit [IsProper C.hom]` is informative rather than cosmetic: the implication is pure
430	quantifier weakening — instantiate the single `b` at each `κ` — so it needs no properness, and
431	the linter caught that.  It confirms the two statements differ *only* in quantifier order, with
432	no geometry in between. -/
433	theorem vanishing_baseChangeField_of_uniformVanishing (h : UniformVanishing C)
434	    (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
435	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
436	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
437	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
438	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
439	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
440	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
441	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
442	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1) := by
443	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := h
444	  exact ⟨b, hb κ⟩
445	
446	end OpenHalf
447	
448	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	# Extension-uniformity: the free half WITNESSED, and the open half reduced to one scalar
11	
12	`Ledger/FiberBound.lean` closes cluster-P items 1 and 3 over a *single* field `k`, and its
13	closing section says extension-uniformity splits into a free half and an open half.  That
14	section states the free half as a property of three **morphism classes**
15	(`baseChange_binders_stable`: `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and
16	`GeometricallyIrreducible` are each stable under base change).  That is true, and it is not
17	the same statement as "the vanishing theorem re-fires at the base-changed curve": a class
18	being stable under base change says nothing until some object is exhibited carrying the
19	base-changed instances, in the spelling the consuming theorem actually elaborates against.
20	
21	This file supplies the object.  `Scheme.baseChangeField C κ` (`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean`)
22	is AJC's named base-changed curve `C_κ = C ×_{Spec k} Spec κ`, and it already carries
23	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIntegral` as **named instances**.
24	One instance was missing from that stack — `GeometricallyIrreducible`, which is what the
25	`Ledger` curve statements bind — and `geometricallyIrreducible_hom_baseChangeField` below adds
26	it.  With it, every curve-level statement of `FiberBound` applies to `C_κ` **by instance
27	synthesis alone**, at base field `κ`, with no new mathematics and no hypothesis on `κ/k`: not
28	finiteness, not separability, not perfectness.
29	
30	## What is proved here, and what is deliberately not
31	
32	* `vanishing_baseChangeField` / `riemannRoch_baseChangeField` — the **free half, witnessed**:
33	  a threshold `b(κ)` exists at `C_κ` for every `κ`, and exact Riemann–Roch holds above it with
34	  the base-changed genus `genus C_κ`.  This is the honest content of "the theorem re-fires per
35	  field", now stated at an object rather than about a class.
36	* `UniformVanishing` — the **open half, named as a definition** so that consumers can quantify
37	  over it and so that its exact quantifier order is inspectable: `∃ b, ∀ κ, ∀ D on C_κ, …`.
38	  The `b` is chosen **before** `κ`.  This is *not* proved here and this file does not claim it.
39	* `uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` — the **reduction**: the open half
40	  follows from exactly **two** inputs, a uniform degree bound on a vanishing base divisor and
41	  base-field invariance of the genus.  Neither is proved here; both are named precisely.
42	  **Update:** the genus input is now proved in `Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.lean`, so prefer
43	  `GenusFieldInvariance.uniformVanishing_of_uniformBaseDivisor`, which needs only the first.
44	* `exists_deg_ge` — **non-vacuity**: degrees are unbounded above given one closed point of
45	  positive residue degree, so a degree half-space is never empty and `UniformVanishing` is not
46	  trivially satisfiable by having no instances.  Proved.
47	
48	## What the constant actually decomposes into (correcting my own earlier account)
49	
50	`FiberBound`'s closing docstring located the obstruction in the constant: `b(κ)` is built from
51	`n₀(κ)`, a `Classical.choose` on a Noetherian stabilization re-run at each base field, and
52	nothing relates `n₀(κ)` to `n₀(k)`.  That describes the *proof*, not the *problem*.  The
53	threshold produced by `DegreeVanishing.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one` is
54	
55	`b = deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪)`,
56	
57	and that existential is **monotone in `b`** (a `D` of degree `≥ b'` has degree `≥ b` whenever
58	`b ≤ b'`).  So `n₀` itself never has to transport: it suffices to bound `b(κ)` above by
59	something independent of `κ`.  Since `χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = 1 − genus C_κ` (`ChiCurve.chi_moduleKSheaf`
60	composed with `GenusBridge.ledgerGenus_eq_genus`, both at `C_κ` — this is checked, not assumed),
61	
62	`b(κ) = deg_κ D₀(κ) + genus C_κ`,
63	
64	which exposes **two** `κ`-dependencies, not one:
65	
66	1. `genus C_κ` — a scalar, addressed by base-field invariance of the genus;
67	2. `deg_κ D₀(κ)` — the degree of the base divisor, where `D₀(κ) = n₀(κ) • F_κ`.  This is where
68	   the `Classical.choose` survives, and bounding it is *not* a corollary of (1).
69	
70	**A retraction.**  An earlier version of this docstring said the threshold "can be taken to be
71	`2g − 1`", which would have collapsed (2) into (1) and made the genus identity the whole
72	residue.  That is standard curve theory but it is **not available here**: `deg D ≥ 2g − 1 ⟹
73	H¹ = 0` goes through Serre duality, and there is **no Serre duality, canonical divisor or
74	dualizing sheaf anywhere in this workspace** — searched across AJC, AJCR and mathlib, which
75	has no Serre duality for curves at all.  So the reduction below carries both hypotheses.  I
76	had published the one-input version on the team thread before checking it; this is the
77	corrected form.
78

274	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=

### Judge's additional finding (adopted into the plan)

**P5/M3 (uniform H¹ vanishing) has a duality-free, field-uniform proof that shrinks it from XL to L–XL**, resolving the one place where D1's "avoid duality" critique of the Milne route had bite:
- `i(D) := h¹(O(D))` is monotone decreasing under adding points (from `0 → O(D) → O(D+p) → κ(p) → 0`).
- Pick `n₀` over the base field `k` with `h¹(C, O(n₀·x₀)) = 0` (single-bundle Serre-type vanishing; in reach of the adelic lane's finiteness + `HasFiniteMapToP1` machinery). Flat base change makes this bound **uniform over all field extensions κ/k**: `h¹(C_κ, O(n₀·x₀)_κ) = 0`.
- For any invertible `M` on `C_κ` with `deg M ≥ n₀·deg(x₀) + g`: `h⁰(M(−n₀x₀)) ≥ χ = deg − n₀ − g + 1 ≥ 1` (Riemann inequality direction of P3, no duality), so `M ≅ O(n₀x₀ + E)` with `E ≥ 0`, hence `h¹(M) ≤ h¹(O(n₀x₀)_κ) = 0`.
This discharges the ∃-form bound `b := n₀ + g` exactly as D3 pinned it, with the rational point supplying the ample divisor — a use of `[HasRationalPoint C]` all three designs missed. Fallbacks: D1's `C^d`-family trick; Clifford over `κ̄` (last resort, scope-creep warning).

---

## Part II — THE PLAN

**Architecture**: D3's Milne–Kollár route (section trick on the Div substrate + finite Galois quotient + coproduct assembly), with grafts: D2's M0/Γ-stable-cover/orbit-in-affine/separability/hygiene; D1's audit discipline and fallback tricks; new milestone B6 (separatedness device); P5 via the judge's uniform elementary route.

Fixed notation: `g := h¹(C, O)`; `x₀` the rational point; `b` the P5 bound; `r` chosen with `r ≥ b` and `r ≥ 2g+1` (classically `r = 2g+1`); `k'` runs over finite Galois subextensions of `k^s/k`; Λ = the four instance hypotheses of `instHasPicScheme`.

Sizes: S ≤ 1 session, M ≈ 1–2, L ≈ 3–5, XL ≥ 6.

(ii) `RiemannRoch/Adelic/GateInstances.lean`. (iii) trdeg-1 function field; in-lane substrate. (iv) **M**. /-!
# Quasi-coherence packaging of the divisor sheaves `𝒪(D)`

The divisor sheaves of the curve bundle satisfy the quasi-coherence packaging `Scheme.QcohOn`
of `Ledger/QcohSections.lean` on **every** open `U`, so the twisted affine Serre vanishing
(`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_hModule'_one_of_qcoh`, `Ledger/AffineVanishingQcoh.lean`) fires on
them over every affine open.  That is what discharges the two affine-vanishing instances the
two-cover `H¹` carrier consumes at the chart preimages `V₀`, `V₁`.

## Provenance

AJCR `RiemannRoch/FLVQcoh.lean`, bodies unchanged.  **This file is the empirical confirmation
of the port audit**: AJCR imports it against `Picard/PresentationDivisor.lean`, and that edge —
the single entry point of AJCR's fourteen-module `Picard.*` presentation cone into the vanishing
chain — turned out to be needed only for the `coeffAt` calculus, which
`Ledger/FiberDivisor.lean` now carries.  Substituting that import for the Picard one, the file
elaborates with **no other change**: no `picClass`, no `CechPic`, no meromorphic presentation.
So the cone was bundling, not dependency, and the claim is now checked rather than argued.

For the curve bundle `X` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over
a field `K`) and a Weil divisor `D`:

* **(P1) action.** An ambient section `r : Γ(X, U)` acts on `𝒪(D)(W)` for `W ≤ U` by
  multiplication with its germ at the generic point: `ord_x (germ_η r) ≤ 1` at every closed
  `x ∈ U` (`Scheme.ord_algebraMap_stalk_le_one` through the germ/stalk seam), so the pole
  bounds of `D` are preserved. Naturality under restriction is automatic: restrictions of
  `𝒪(D)`-sections are inclusions of submodules of `K(X)`.
* **(P2a) denominator clearing** is ord bookkeeping: `germ_η g` has order `0` on `D(g)`
  (`Scheme.ord_eq_one_of_mem_basicOpen`) and order `≥ 1` at the finitely many zeros of `g`
  (the divisor `div (germ_η g)` is finitely supported), so a large power of `g` clears the
  poles of any section of `𝒪(D)(V ⊓ D(g))` along `V ∖ D(g)` — the same pole-clearing
  pattern as the lattice exhaustion `iSup_fiberLattice` of `Ledger/FiberLattice.lean`.
* **(P2b) defect annihilation is degenerate** for this family: restrictions between
  nonempty opens are injective, and when `V ⊓ D(g)` is empty while `V` is not, the germ
  `germ_η g` is a non-unit of the function *field*, hence zero — so `g` itself annihilates.

The empty-open corners are absorbed by the `⊥`-guard of `Scheme.divisorSections`; when `U`
does not contain the generic point (i.e. `U = ∅`), all section modules over `W ≤ U` are
zero and the packaging is trivial.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.divisorSheaf.instQcohOn` — the instance
  `Scheme.QcohOn (X.divisorSheaf K D) U`, for every open `U`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_hModule'_divisorSheaf_one` — the discharge:
  `Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' (X.divisorSheaf K D) U 1)` for affine `U`. This is the pair of
  vanishing instances the two-cover H¹ carrier (`Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv`) consumes at the
  chart preimages `V₀`, `V₁` in `Ledger/FiberVanishing.lean`.
-/

### Judge's additional finding (adopted into the plan)

**P5/M3 (uniform H¹ vanishing) has a duality-free, field-uniform proof that shrinks it from XL to L–XL**, resolving the one place where D1's "avoid duality" critique of the Milne route had bite:
- `i(D) := h¹(O(D))` is monotone decreasing under adding points (from `0 → O(D) → O(D+p) → κ(p) → 0`).
- Pick `n₀` over the base field `k` with `h¹(C, O(n₀·x₀)) = 0` (single-bundle Serre-type vanishing; in reach of the adelic lane's finiteness + `HasFiniteMapToP1` machinery). Flat base change makes this bound **uniform over all field extensions κ/k**: `h¹(C_κ, O(n₀·x₀)_κ) = 0`.
- For any invertible `M` on `C_κ` with `deg M ≥ n₀·deg(x₀) + g`: `h⁰(M(−n₀x₀)) ≥ χ = deg − n₀ − g + 1 ≥ 1` (Riemann inequality direction of P3, no duality), so `M ≅ O(n₀x₀ + E)` with `E ≥ 0`, hence `h¹(M) ≤ h¹(O(n₀x₀)_κ) = 0`.
This discharges the ∃-form bound `b := n₀ + g` exactly as D3 pinned it, with the rational point supplying the ample divisor — a use of `[HasRationalPoint C]` all three designs missed. Fallbacks: D1's `C^d`-family trick; Clifford over `κ̄` (last resort, scope-creep warning).

---

## Part II — THE PLAN

**Architecture**: D3's Milne–Kollár route (section trick on the Div substrate + finite Galois quotient + coproduct assembly), with grafts: D2's M0/Γ-stable-cover/orbit-in-affine/separability/hygiene; D1's audit discipline and fallback tricks; new milestone B6 (separatedness device); P5 via the judge's uniform elementary route.

Fixed notation: `g := h¹(C, O)`; `x₀` the rational point; `b` the P5 bound; `r` chosen with `r ≥ b` and `r ≥ 2g+1` (classically `r = 2g+1`); `k'` runs over finite Galois subextensions of `k^s/k`; Λ = the four instance hypotheses of `instHasPicScheme`.

Sizes: S ≤ 1 session, M ≈ 1–2, L ≈ 3–5, XL ≥ 6.

### Milestone DAG

#### Cluster P — curve cohomology kit (reuse the adelic lane)

**P1 — Discharge the adelic lane's gates.**
(i) Instances for `ExistsNonconstantMapToP1 C` (**since discharged**: `existsNonconstantMapToProjInt_of_ajc` and `existsNonconstantMapToP1_of_existsNonconstantMapToProjInt`, `RiemannRoch/Adelic/NonconstantToP1.lean`, so the whole chain to `HasFiniteMapToP1` synthesises for an AJC curve) and `P1HasLaurentChartData`; audit whether the `HasExt`-shaped inputs are already unconditional in `CechComparisonGate.lean:114-136`.
(ii) `RiemannRoch/Adelic/GateInstances.lean`. (iii) trdeg-1 function field; in-lane substrate. (iv) **M**. (v) 🔍 **AUDIT-FIRST**: kernel-build the whole `RiemannRoch/` closure before relying on "sorry-free" (memory lesson: verify inherited closures; the lane's only true sorry must remain `WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`, off-path).

**P2 — h⁰/h¹/χ kit over all field extensions.**
(i) For every field κ/k and invertible `M` on `C_κ`: `h0 κ M`, `h1 κ M : ℕ` finite; pinned on the **Čech carrier** (`AffineCoverMVSquare`, `RiemannRoch/Adelic/Substrate.lean`) with cover-independence proved Čech-to-Čech (structurally avoids the `HasCechToHModuleIso` gate); flat-base-change stability `h^i(C_κ, M) = h^i(C_{κ'}, M_{κ'})`.
(ii) `RiemannRoch/CohomologyKit.lean`. (iii) P1; `GenusFiniteness.lean:64`. (iv) **L**. (v) 🔍 AUDIT: Λ-stability instances for `C_κ` (smooth proper geometrically integral over κ) + base-change of `AffineCoverMVSquare` — record as named lemmas, don't inline.

**P3 — Riemann–Roch χ-ledger.**
(i) `χ(M) = deg M + 1 − g` with `deg` the residue-weighted Weil degree (`RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean:1047`); point-sequence induction from `χ(O) = 1 − g`; `M ≅ O(div s)` for `0 ≠ s ∈ H⁰` (integrality ⟹ regular section). Byproduct: closes the input to the `WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` sorry (off-path bonus).
(ii) `RiemannRoch/RiemannRochChi.lean`. (iii) P2; `WeilDivisor.lean` linear equivalence :1471. (iv) **L**. (v) 🔍 AUDIT: degree invariance under linear equivalence over **non-perfect** κ — keep the residue-field-weighted convention.

**P4 — h⁰ bounds, drops, rational-point density.**
(i) (a) `deg < 0 ⟹ h⁰ = 0`; (b) `h⁰ > 0 ⟹ h⁰ ≤ deg + 1`; (c) κ **separably closed**, `h⁰ ≥ 2` ⟹ ∃ rational x with exact drop `h⁰(M(−x)) = h⁰(M) − 1` (evaluation map at a rational non-base point); (d) closed points of `C_κ` (κ sep. closed) are rational and dense (smooth ⟹ separable residue fields).

**P5 — Uniform H¹ vanishing (∃-form pin).**
(i) `∃ b, ∀ κ/k, ∀ M invertible on C_κ, b ≤ deg M → h1 κ M = 0 ∧ GloballyGenerated M`. **Primary route (judge's)**: `i(D)`-monotonicity + one Serre-type vanishing `h¹(O(n₀x₀)) = 0` over `k` + flat base change of the bound + `h⁰(M(−n₀x₀)) ≥ 1` from P3 ⟹ `b := n₀ + g` works uniformly. (ii) `RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean`; gate `HasH1VanishingBound C b`. (iii) P2–P4; `[HasRationalPoint C]` (supplies `x₀`, the ample divisor). (iv) **L–XL** (down from D2/D3's XL). Fallback 2: Clifford over κ̄.

#### Cluster B — base-change engines over the constant curve

(ii) `Picard/PicSharpZariskiSheaf.lean`. (iii) B0; `RelPicFunctor.lean:582/:702/:1004/:1057`; `HasRationalPoint` (:139). (iv) **L**. (v) 🔍 AUDIT: FALSE without the section (docstring `FGAPicRepresentability.lean:35-59`) — `[HasRationalPoint C]` in every pin.

**B2 — Filtered-colimit reduction brick.**
(i) On affine `T = Spec A`, `A = colim A_i` (f.g. k-subalgebras): invertible sheaves on `C_A` (2-affine cocycle presentation), `DivFamily`s, and picSharp-class equalities descend to some `A_i`; picSharp/`DivFunctorDeg` restricted to affines preserve filtered colimits.

**B3 — THE rigid pushforward engine (hardest single lemma).**
(i) `pushforward_locallyFree_of_h1_vanishing`: A f.g. 363	/-- **Global generation at `P` from the two vanishings** — `evalMap_surjective`
364	composed with `generatedAt_of_evalMap_surjective`.
365	
366	**Conjunction audit** (the check memory I-0399 requires for this task, run for this
367	theorem): the hypotheses are *not* equivalent to the conclusion, so this is a reduction
368	and not a re-indexing.  `GeneratedAt k D P` yields a section attaining the bound at `P`,
369	which is exactly the statement that some section of `𝒪(D)` is **not** a section of
370	`𝒪(D − P)` — i.e. a *strict* drop `ℓ(D − P) < ℓ(D)`.  The hypotheses give the **maximal**
371	drop `ℓ(D) − ℓ(D − P) = [κ(P):k]`.  Those differ as soon as `[κ(P):k] ≥ 2`, so the
372	converse fails and the vanishing input is doing real work.  (Over an algebraically closed
373	base they coincide, which is the degenerate case, not the general one.) -/
374	theorem generatedAt_of_vanishing
375	    (D : X.WeilDivisor) (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
376	    (hledgerD : chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
377	    (hledgerDP : chi k U₀ U₁ (D - pointDivisor P) =
378	      chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k (D - pointDivisor P))
379	    (hD : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D))
380	    (hDP : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ (D - pointDivisor P)))
381	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)]
382	    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
383	    GeneratedAt k D P :=
384	  generatedAt_of_evalMap_surjective k D P
385	    (evalMap_surjective k U₀ U₁ D P hledgerD hledgerDP hD hDP)
386	
387	end GeneratedAt
388	
389	/-! ## §4. The threshold: how far above the vanishing bound
390	
391	`generatedAt_of_vanishing` needs vanishing at `D` *and* at `D − P`.  Feeding it the
392	bounded-vanishing theorem requires both divisors above the threshold `b`, and
393	
394	`deg_k (D − P) = deg_k D − [κ(P):k]`,
395	
396	so the generation threshold is `b + [κ(P):k]` — the vanishing bound raised by the
397	residue degree **at that point**.  Two forms follow.
398	
399	*Pointwise* (`exists_bound_generatedAt`): for each `P` separately, no extra hypothesis.
400	
401	*Uniform* (`exists_bound_forall_generatedAt`): the same `D` generating at
402	**every** `P` at once needs a uniform bound `r` on residue degrees, `∀ P, [κ(P):k] ≤ r`.
403	That is a real hypothesis and not a formality: over a finite field the residue degrees
404	of closed points are unbounded, so no such `r` exists there, whereas over an
405	algebraically closed base `r = 1` works.  This is the precise sense in which global
406	generation is "the bound raised by the maximum residue degree" — and the maximum has to
407	exist.
408	-/
409	
410	section Threshold
411	
412	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
413	    [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
414	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
415	
416	/-- **Global generation above the shifted bound, pointwise in `P`.**
417	
418	Given the three inputs of `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` there is a threshold `b`
419	such that for every `P` and every `D` with `deg_k D ≥ b + [κ(P):k]`, the sheaf `𝒪(D)`
420	is generated by global sections at `P`.
421	
422	The shift by `[κ(P):k]` is exactly what puts `D − P` above `b` as well; it is not
423	slack. -/
424	theorem exists_bound_generatedAt
425	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
426	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
427	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,
428	      (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
429	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
430	      Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D')
431	    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)]
432	    [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
433	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (D : X.WeilDivisor) (P : X.PrimeDivisor),
434	      b + residueDeg k P ≤ degK k D → GeneratedAt k D P := by
435	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ :=
436	    exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase hpeel
437	  refine ⟨b, fun D P hD => ?_⟩
438	  have hdegDP : degK k (D - pointDivisor P) = degK k D - residueDeg k P := by
439	    rw [degK_sub, degK_pointDivisor]
440	  exact generatedAt_of_vanishing k U₀ U₁ D P (hledger D)
441	    (hledger (D - pointDivisor P)) (hb D (by omega))
442	    (hb (D - pointDivisor P) (by omega))
443	
444	/-- **Uniform global generation above the shifted bound.**  With a uniform bound `r` on
445	residue degrees, one threshold `b + r` works for **every** point at once: above it,
446	`𝒪(D)` is generated by global sections at every prime divisor.
447	
448	This is the strongest global-generation statement reachable in AJC today.  It remains
449	**single-field** — `k`, the cover `U₀, U₁` and `D₀` are all fixed, and nothing here
450	quantifies over field extensions, so extension uniformity is untouched (gap 2 of the
451	module docstring). -/
452	theorem exists_bound_forall_generatedAt
453	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
454	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
455	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,
456	      (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
457	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
458	      Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D')
459	    (r : ℕ) (hr : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, residueDeg k P ≤ r)
460	    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)]
461	    [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
462	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
463	      ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, GeneratedAt k D P := by
464	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ :=
465	    exists_bound_generatedAt k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase hpeel
466	  refine ⟨b + r, fun D hD P => ?_⟩
467	  refine hb D P ?_
468	  have := hr P
469	  omega
470	
471	end Threshold
